newsitem.title: USA: Belco Oil sets Wyoming exploration.
newsitem.headline: Belco Oil sets Wyoming exploration.

text.p: Belco Oil & Gas Corp said Tuesday it has reached two agreements to fund exploration in Wyoming in return for stakes in the leases being developed.
It estimated spending this year associated with these deals is likely to be in the $7.5-to-$12.5 million range.
The company said agreeemts with Andover Partners and Andex Partners, private exploration groups, will form a joint exploration program the Green River and Wind River basins.
Belco said it will acquire a 50 percent interest in some 553,000 gross and 300,000 net mineral acres after exploration funding totaling $20 million over the next five years.
Costs in excess of $20 million will be shared equally by Belco and its partners.

Yates Petroleum Corp, a private exploration and production company, is a major working interest owner in this acreage and is expected to operate many of the wells in the initial phases of this program. Union Pacific Resources Group Inc will also operate certain wells for the venture and is currently drilling the initial well.
Belco said it also agreed with Snyder Oil Corp to form two development programs in the Wind River and Bighorn basins of Wyoming.

One covers 63,408 gross and 63,364 net acres in the Otto Area of the Bighorn Basin where will acquire a 50 percent working interest. The cost of drilling the initial well will be shared equally. Snyder will be the operator and expects to commence drilling February 1.
Belco said it will have the option to purchase a 50 percent working interest in an additional 55,626 gross and 47,496 net acres in prospect areas nearby.

The program covers 30,692 gross and 30,444 net acres in the North Riverton area of the Wind River Basin. Belco will acquire a 50 percent working interest and will pay 100 percent of the cost to drill and complete the initial well limited to a cap of $1,087,900. Thereafter, the costs will be shared equally. Snyder expects to commence drilling the initial well prior to May 1.
Belco said it will also have the option to purchase an undivided 50 percent working interest in an additional 57,923 gross and 56,918 net acres in the Wind River Basin.
The company said it views these agreements as important
steps in its efforts to enhance its existing core area holdings in Wyoming.

Belco said it believes these deals are attractive "given the substantial increase in Rocky Mountain (natural) gas prices in recent months, the long-lived nature of these assets and the potential for hundreds of locations which the acreage may hold in the coming years." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
